Romans 13:1–2 (KJV)
“Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.

Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.”

The exception is when human laws conflict with God’s commands. The apostles demonstrated this in:

Acts 5:29 (KJV)
“Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.”

So the biblical principle is:
* Obey civil government and its laws (Romans 13:1–7).
* Submit to every ordinance of man (1 Peter 2:13–17).
* Pay taxes and give proper honor (Matthew 22:21; Romans 13:6–7).
* But if government commands something contrary to God’s will, obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29).

That’s why something can be legal and still be morally wrong. Legality is determined by human governments; morality is determined by God. Scripture calls some things sinful even when governments permit them, and Scripture also requires Christians to obey lawful authority unless doing so would require disobedience to God.
